name: Soft Circuit
description: Subtle fixed offsets for soft pads and restrained synth chords.
listening_hint: Try a simple C minor or A minor chord; compare with 12 EDO using a sustained sound.

name: Loose Clock
description: Small irregular offsets for bass sequences and dry plucks.
listening_hint: Try a repeating C, Eb, G, Bb pattern.

name: Glass Steps
description: Lowered thirds with raised neighboring notes for glassy arpeggios and synth chords.
listening_hint: Try C, E, G, Bb with a bright, harmonically rich patch.

name: Bent Fifths
description: A narrowed C-G fifth introduces tension into otherwise familiar shapes.
listening_hint: Try sustained C-G dyads or a two-note bass ostinato.

name: Split Neon
description: Alternating offsets make neighboring steps expand and contract. C and A stay fixed as tonal anchors.
listening_hint: Try chromatic plucks or a short repeating sequence.

name: Oxide
description: Stronger irregular offsets for tense pads, rough-edged stabs, and sparse melodies.
listening_hint: Try C, Eb, F, G, Bb with long releases to expose the changing intervals.

name: Ripple
description: Groups of rising offsets followed by a reset give scalar lines an uneven contour.
listening_hint: Try ascending semitones on a clean pluck before moving to a longer sequence.

name: Warped Grid
description: Pronounced opposing offsets for angular leads and dissonant chord fragments. Octaves remain exact even as the intervals inside them pull apart.
listening_hint: Start with two or three notes.

name: Frayed Thirds
description: A nearly pure C–G fifth frames a widened C–E third and narrowed C–Eb third.
listening_hint: Hold C–G, then add E or Eb to hear the extra beating.

name: Restless Fifths
description: A nearly pure C–E major third meets a narrowed C–G fifth.
listening_hint: Hold C–E, then add G. Try a sustained saw or pulse sound.
